text:
Eastern Townships theatre artists bring Daniel MacIvor’s ‘The Best Brothers’ to Montreal in Quebec premiere
Events
Thom Niles, artistic producer of Born on a Raft Theatre and star of The Best Brothers, which opens May 28 in Montreal. (Photo: courtesy)
Get local news like this every morning. Subscribe free below.
A new Montreal theatre company with deep roots in Quebec’s Eastern Townships is taking to the stage for the first time this month, bringing a celebrated Canadian play to Quebec audiences for the very first time.
Born on a Raft Theatre will present the Quebec premiere of Daniel MacIvor’s The Best Brothers at White Wall Studio, 4532 Avenue Laval, Montreal, running May 28 to 31 at 8 p.m. nightly. The production runs approximately 80 minutes and marks the inaugural show for the newly formed company, which is registered with both ELAN and the Quebec Drama Federation.
A press release states that the dark comedy follows brothers Kyle and Hamilton Best as they navigate the aftermath of their mother’s sudden death — killed in a freak accident involving a drag queen named Pina Colada — while sorting out final arrangements, old resentments, and the perennial sibling question of who was Mom’s favourite. The central conflict is as much about grief as it is about the dog their mother clearly loved more than either of them.
The production stars Montreal actor Thom Niles alongside Sam Beaton, a young actor originally from Coaticook who began his working life as a welder in the family business before pivoting to a career in theatre and television. The director is Trevor Barrette, a META award-winning director. Rounding out the creative team are stage manager Orlando Lopez, designer Natalie Demmon — herself a Bishop’s University alumna in drama and music — and composer Violette Kay.
The Townships connections run through much of the production. Niles, the company’s artistic producer, studied drama at Bishop’s University before going on to the University of Worcester’s Drama and Performance Program. Originally from Labrador, he spent years working in Halifax with DaPoPo Theatre, Zuppa Works, and the Halifax Fringe Festival before settling in Montreal. At the 2023 Montreal Fringe, he earned rave reviews for his performance in Heartbeast, which won the Patron’s Pick award.
Niles said the shared background among cast and crew gives the production a particular chemistry. “This piece is magical, and I believe a lot of that comes from the shared camaraderie we have as people with roots in the Townships,” he wrote in a note to The Pulse.
Born on a Raft Theatre’s name draws on a Newfoundland and Labrador expression — asking someone who leaves a door open if they were “born on a raft” — which the company takes as a symbol of leaving the door open for opportunity and embracing the quirks that define them as artists. The company’s stated mission is to promote Atlantic Canadian playwrights and tell queer stories using Montreal-based performers, filling a gap Niles identified after years in the city’s independent theatre scene.
Tickets and more information are available at bornonarafttheatre.com or by contacting Thomas Niles at bornonarafttheatre@gmail.com or 438-529-1734.
